questions.q: The elastic behaviour of material for linear stress and linear strain, is shown in the figure. The energy density for a linear strain of $5 \times {10}^{- 4}$ is _____ $kJ{m}^{- 3}$. Assume that material is elastic upto the linear strain of $5 \times {10}^{- 4}$,
questions.solution:
From the above graph, we can find that when the strain is $5 \times {10}^{- 4}$ the stress is $100MPa$. We know that energy density is

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times stress \times strain$$⇒ U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 \times {10}^{6} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ U = 2 . 5 \times {10}^{4}J{m}^{- 3} = 25kJ{m}^{- 3}$

questions.q: When a long glass capillary tube of radius $0 . 015cm$ is dipped in a liquid, the liquid rises to a height of $15cm$ within it. If the contact angle between the liquid and glass to close to $0 °$, the surface tension of the liquid, in milliNewton ${m}^{- 1},$ is $\left[{ρ}_{\text{(liqued)}} = 900kg{m}^{- 3}, g = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right]$ (Given answer in closed integer)
questions.solution:
Using the concept of rise due to surface tension,

$\dfrac{2T}{r} = hρg$

$T = \dfrac{rhρg}{2} = \dfrac{15 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 15 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 900 \times 10}{2} = 101milliNewton{m}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A hydraulic press can lift $100kg$ when a mass $m$ is placed on the smaller piston. It can lift kg when the diameter of the larger piston is increased by $4$ times and that of the smaller piston is decreased by $4$ times keeping the same mass $m$ on the smaller piston.
questions.solution:
Using Pascals law,

$\dfrac{100 \times g}{{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{mg}{{A}_{1}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Let $m$ mass can lift ${M}_{0}$ in second case then

$\dfrac{{M}_{0}g}{16{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{mg}{{A}_{1} / 16} . . . \left(2\right)$

$\left\{SinceA = \dfrac{\pi{d}^{2}}{4}\right\}$

From equation $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$ we get

$\dfrac{{M}_{0}}{16 . 100} = 16$

$⇒ {M}_{0} = 25600kg$

questions.q: A square aluminium (shear modulus is $25 \times {10}^{9}{Nm}^{- 2}$) slab of side $60cm$ and thickness $15cm$ is subjected to a shearing force (on its narrow face) of $18 . 0 \times {10}^{4}N$. The lower edge is riveted to the floor. The displacement of the upper edge is _____ $\mum$.
questions.solution:
Shearing stress is given by $\dfrac{F}{A} = η\dfrac{x}{l}$

Thus, displacement is $x = \dfrac{Fl}{Aη}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{18 \times {10}^{4} \times 60 \times {10}^{- 2}}{60 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 15 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 25 \times {10}^{9}}$

$= 48 \times {10}^{- 6}m = 48\mum$

questions.q: In an experiment to determine the Young's modulus, steel wires of five different lengths ($1, 2, 3, 4$ and $5$) but of same cross-section $\left(2{mm}^{2}\right)$ were taken and curves between extension and load were obtained. The slope (extension/load) of the curves were plotted with the wire length and the following graph is obtained. If the Young's modulus of given steel wires is $x \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$, then the value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
We know that, Young's modulus is $Y = \dfrac{FL}{A ∆ L}$, where, $F$ is force or load acting on wire, $A$ is cross-section area, $L$ is length and $∆ L$ is extension in length.

Now, from given graph, the slope of the line is $= \dfrac{\dfrac{\DeltaL}{W}}{L} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\DeltaL}{L}}{W} = \dfrac{1}{YA}$

$⇒ Y = \dfrac{1}{\left(slope\right)A}$

Thus, Young's modulus of the steel wires is $Y = \dfrac{1}{2 \times {10}^{- 6}\left(0 . 25 \times {10}^{- 5}\right)}$

$⇒ Y = 2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$.

Therefore, $x = 2$.

questions.q: Two wires each of radius $0 . 2cm$ and negligible mass, one made of steel and the other made of brass are loaded as shown in the figure. The elongation of the steel wire is ______${10}^{– 6}m$. [Young's modulus for steel $= 2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{– 2}$ and $g = 10m{s}^{– 2}$]
questions.solution:
The force acting on steel wire $F$ is $\left(2 + 1 . 14\right)g = 3 . 14g$

From the relation of Young's modulus, it can be written

$\dfrac{F}{A} = Y\left(\dfrac{\DeltaL}{L}\right)$

$⇒ \DeltaL = \left(\dfrac{FL}{AY}\right) = \dfrac{3 . 14 \times g \times 1 . 6}{\pi \times {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} \times 2 \times {10}^{11} \times {10}^{- 4}}$

$⇒ ∆ L = 2 \times {10}^{- 5}$

$⇒ ∆ L = 20 \times {10}^{- 6}m$

questions.q: The potential energy of a particle of mass $4kg$ in motion along the $x$-axis is given by $U = 4\left(1 - cos4x\right)J$. The time period of the particle for small oscillation $\left(sin\theta ≃ \theta\right)$ $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{K}\right)s$. The value of $K$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Given here, potential energy, $U = 4\left(1 - cos4x\right)J$

Using the relation between conservative force and potential energy, $F = - \dfrac{d U}{d x}$.

We have, $F = - 4\left(+ sin4x\right)4 = - 16sin\left(4x\right)$

For small $\theta$, $sin\theta \approx \theta$.

Acceleration of particle is $a = - \dfrac{64x}{m} = \dfrac{- 64x}{4} = - 16x$

As the oscillations are simple harmonic in nature, so $a = - {\omega}^{2}x ⇒ {\omega}^{2} = 16 ⇒ \omega = 4rad{s}^{- 1}$

Now, time period of oscillation is$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Thus, the value of $K = 2$.

questions.q: In the figure given below. a block of mass $M = 490g$ placed on a frictionless table is connected with two springs having same spring constant ($K = 2N{m}^{- 1}$). If the block is horizontally displaced through $X$ $m$ then the number of complete oscillations it will make in $14\pi$ seconds will be ______.
questions.solution:
Both the springs are connected in parallel, therefore

${K}_{eq} = K + K = 2K$

Now, time period of spring-block system is given by,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2K}}$

Given here, $m = 490gm$$= 0 . 49kg$ and $K = 2N{m}^{- 1}$

So, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 49}{2 \times 2}}$

$= 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{49}{400}} = 2\pi\dfrac{7}{20} = \dfrac{7\pi}{10}$

Now, number of oscillation in $14\pi$ is

$N = \dfrac{time}{T} = \dfrac{14\pi}{\dfrac{7\pi}{10}} = 20$

questions.q: The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive $x$-direction is given by $y = \dfrac{1}{( 1 + x{)}^{2}}$ at time $t = 0$ and $y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - 2{)}^{2}}$ at $t = 1s$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be $m{s}^{- 1} .$
questions.solution:
At $t = 0, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + {x}^{2}}$
At time $t = t, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - vt{)}^{2}}$
At $t = 1, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - v{)}^{2}} \ldots ( i )$
At $t = 1, y = \dfrac{1}{1 + ( x - 2{)}^{2}} \ldots ( ii )$
Comparing $( i ) and ( ii )$
$v = 2m{s}^{- 1}$

They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by $y = \left(10cos\pixsin\dfrac{2\pit}{T}\right)cm$. The amplitude of the particle at $x = \dfrac{4}{3}cm$ will be _____ $cm .$

Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position, for that

Therefore, $A = \left|10cos\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\right)\right| = 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 5cm$

questions.q: The first overtone frequency of an open organ pipe is equal to the fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe. If the length of the closed organ pipe is $20cm$. The length of the open organ pipe is _____ $cm$
questions.solution:
The fundamental frequency of the closed organ pipe is given by, ${f}_{0} = \dfrac{v}{4{l}_{c}}$.

The frequency of the first overtone of a open organ pipe is given by, ${f}_{1} = 2 \times \dfrac{v}{2{l}_{o}}$.

Since,

${f}_{0} = {f}_{1} ⇒ \dfrac{v}{4{l}_{c}} = \dfrac{v}{{l}_{o}} ⇒ {l}_{o} = 4 \times 20 = 80cm$.

questions.q: A set of $20$ tuning forks is arranged in a series of increasing frequencies. If each fork gives $4$ beats with respect to the preceding fork and the frequency of the last fork is twice the frequency of the first, then the frequency of last fork is _____ $Hz$.
questions.solution:
Each fork produces $4$ beats per second with the previous means each fork has frequency $4Hz$ more than the previous.

Using relation, ${f}_{last} = {f}_{first} + \left(N - 1\right)x$, here, $N$ is the number of tuning fork in series and $x$ is beat frequency between two successive forks.

$2{f}_{0} = {f}_{0} + \left(20 - 1\right)4$

$⇒ 2{f}_{0} = {f}_{0} + 76 ⇒ {f}_{0} = 76Hz$

Frequency of last tuning fork is $152Hz$.

questions.q: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of $20 . 0cm$ for a tuning fork of frequency $400Hz$ is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is $336{ms}^{- 1}$. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____ $cm$
questions.solution:
Wavelength of wave $⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{336}{400} = 84cm$

At first resonance

$\dfrac{\lambda}{4} = l + e ⇒ \dfrac{84}{4} = 20 + e$, where, $e$ is end correction.

$⇒ e = 1$
So third resonance length

$5\dfrac{\lambda}{4} = {l}_{2} + e$

$5\left(21\right) = {l}_{2} + 1$

${l}_{2} = 104cm$
